turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: I have no reason to reflect on his misfortunes, for I am not the author of them. You are the last person, Mr. Darcy, who would be concerned for him.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I must confess, Miss Elizabeth, your accusations wound me deeply. Yet, I cannot blame you for your prejudice, for it is a fault I myself have not yet conquered.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your words are kind, Mr. Darcy, but I cannot receive them as such. Your actions towards Mr. Wickham have been a source of pain for me and those I care for.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am aware of the pain my actions have caused, Miss Elizabeth, and I am not proud of them. However, my intentions were not to harm, but to protect.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your intentions may not have been to harm, but your actions spoke otherwise. Mr. Wickham's reputation, my sister's happiness, these are not trivial matters, Mr. Darcy.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your criticisms, though painful, are not unjustified. I am aware of my shortcomings and the harm I have caused. Yet, I find myself compelled to declare my feelings for you, Miss Elizabeth, despite the enmity you justly feel towards me.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your declaration of feelings, Mr. Darcy, comes as a surprise. Yet, your past actions have left me with little room to believe in your sudden change of heart.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Indeed, my past actions have been grievous, and my pride has been my undoing. Yet, I cannot deny the truth of my heart, even if it brings me pain.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: You have indeed caused me much pain, Mr. Darcy, and your past actions have not been those of a gentleman. Yet, your words now challenge my understanding of you.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: My past actions have indeed been reprehensible, and I must bear the consequences of them. Yet, my affections for you, Miss Elizabeth, are sincere and deep.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your words are unexpected, Mr. Darcy, and your past actions make it difficult to accept your sincerity. Yet, I must hear you out.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your regard, Mr. Darcy, is something I have neither sought nor desired, and your past behavior has made any notion of such feelings utterly incomprehensible.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: My regard for you, Miss Elizabeth, is not easily dismissed or forgotten, though I understand your reservations.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your past conduct has been a barrier between us, and your sudden declaration of affection does little to diminish the misunderstandings that have grown between us.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: I am aware of the obstacles that my conduct has erected, yet I cannot deny my feelings or the truth of my heart.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Your past actions have been a source of pain and misunderstanding, Mr. Darcy. How can your words of affection now be anything but a bitter irony?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your words, Elizabeth, are just, and my actions have been deserving of your disdain. Yet, I must try to make amends and express the sincerity of my feelings.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, if you truly believe that a simple declaration of affection can erase the pain you have caused, then you are even more blind to reality than I once thought.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Your accusations, though warranted, do not diminish the truth of my feelings. I must endure the censure of your displeasure, for it is the consequence of my own actions.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy, your actions have consequences that words alone cannot undo. Your pride and prejudice have caused me considerable distress, and I find it difficult to accept your sentiments now.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: In vain have I struggled. It will not do. My feelings will not be repressed. You must allow me to tell you how ardently I admire and love you.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: In such cases as this, it is, I believe, the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned. It is natural that obligation should be felt, and if I could feel gratitude, I would now thank you. But I cannot--I have never desired your good opinion, and you have certainly bestowed it most unwillingly. I am sorry to have occasioned pain to anyone. It has been most unconsciously done, however, and I hope will be of short duration. The feelings which you tell me have long prevented the acknowledgment of your regard can have little difficulty in overcoming it after this explanation.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: And this is all the reply which I am to have the honour of expecting! I might, perhaps, wish to be informed why, with so little endeavour at civility, I am thus rejected. But it is of small importance.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I might as well inquire, why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will, against your reason, and even against your character? Was not this some excuse for incivility, if I was uncivil? But I have other provocations. You know I have. Had not my own feelings decided against you, had they been indifferent, or had they even been favourable, do you think that any consideration would tempt me to accept the man who has been the means of ruining, perhaps for ever, the happiness of a most beloved sister?

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: I have every reason in the world to think ill of you. No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there. You dare not, you cannot deny that you have been the principal, if not the only means of dividing them from each other, of exposing one to the censure of the world for caprice and instability, the other to its derision for disappointed hopes, and involving them both in misery of the acutest kind.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: But it is not merely this affair, on which my dislike is founded. Long before it had taken place, my opinion of you was decided. Your character was unfolded in the recital which I received many months ago from Mr. Wickham. On this subject, what can you have to say? In what imaginary act of friendship can you here defend yourself? or under what misrepresentation can you here impose upon others?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: You take an eager interest in that gentleman’s concerns

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Who that knows what his misfortunes have been can help feeling an interest in him?

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: His misfortunes! yes, his misfortunes have been great indeed.
